item.title: What If World - Stories for Kids - Bonus: What if Mr. Eric was a bronze horse? (from “If Objects Could Talk”)
item.description:
We’re bringing you a bonus episodes from the podcast If Objects Could Talk, The Getty Museum’s first podcast for kids. Mr. Eric voices the bronze horse statuette in this wonderful story, inspired by both art and history. It’s called “Twenty Pounds of Horse Power” and we’ll include their show notes below!
Whether you’re a cowboy, a horse girl, or a simple city slicker, you have to admit that horses are powerful. Why else would nearly every historic leader want their portrait on a horse?
Up on two legs, Adriaen de Vries’s bronze statue Rearing Horse seems to defy the laws of gravity. Even in this dramatic pose, the horse keeps his cool in the podcast studio as he shares about the lost-wax casting process that lets him stand upright and what one school group noticed when they visited him in the Getty galleries.
Like this episode?
Head to the website for a listening guide, where you’ll find discussion topics and related activities, like exploring how hard it is to balance a rearing horse. We also have a coloring page featuring this week’s star!
Teachers, are you working on lessons about story structure? This episode and its listening guide are great resources for the classroom or to send home to families.
If you're enjoying the show, don't forget to leave us a rating or review!
These stories are based on historical research and evidence, but some of the characters and scenarios are fictionalized. If you have questions, write to us or send us a voice memo! You can reach us at PodTeam@getty.edu.
Learn more about the object on our online catalog page: https://www.getty.edu/art/collection/object/103RQZ
For more art history insights, check out our other Getty Podcasts shows at www.getty.edu/podcasts
Recording Artists tells artist biographies using archival material from the Getty Research Institute: https://www.getty.edu/podcasts/recording-artists/
OMMM: Our Museum Mindfulness Meditation merges art history with mindfulness meditations: https://www.getty.edu/podcasts/ommm/
ReCurrent chronicles the people who shape our culture and keep the past alive: https://www.getty.edu/podcasts/recurrent/
Art + Ideas showcases interviews with artists, architects, scientists, and cultural luminaries by former Getty President Jim Cuno: https://www.getty.edu/podcasts/art-and-ideas/
Through its programs—Getty Conservation Institute, Getty Foundation, Getty Museum, Getty Research Institute, and Getty Trust—Getty shares and advances the world’s visual art and cultural heritage, both in Los Angeles and throughout the world.

item.title: Sparkle Stories Podcast - "The Junkyard Feast: A Story of Thanksgiving" from the Junkyard Tales Collection
item.description:
This week's featured story comes from the Junkyard Tales collection. It's called "The Junkyard Feast: A Story of Thanksgiving."

It is time for the annual Junkyard Feast. In this autumn celebration, the Junkyard animals cook special dishes in gratitude for all they have given each other throughout the year. All of the Junkyard animals enjoy this feast except one: Sergeant. He is always away for this special event, celebrating Thanksgiving with the Junkyard Warden and his family. When Ben, clever cat, learns this, he insists they do something special for the steadfast watchdog who keeps the Junkyard safe … all year long.

item.title: Sparkle Stories Podcast - "Graces" from the The Willowbee Tree collection
item.description:
This week's featured story comes from the The Willowbee Tree collection. It's called "Graces."

Little Ty is very silly during dinnertime grace and Clancy doesn't like it. When the two brothers go through the hole in the magical willow tree, they are transported to the highlands of Scotland, long ago — where nothing is attempted without a lovely prayer of honor. A Scottish hare, two badger brothers, and a red kite inspire the boys to remember the importance of saying thanks.

item.title: Sparkle Stories Podcast - "The Lantern Prince" from the So Many Fairies collection
item.description:
This week's featured story comes from the So Many Fairies collection. It's called "The Lantern Prince."

The Prince is not like his parents. In fact, he is not like any royal. In addition to being strong, obedient, and confident — common royal traits — he is also very kind and loving. But what makes the Prince unusual is that he is kind and loving to everyone, royal and servant alike. The King and Queen hope that he will grow out of it, but alas, as he grows he only gets more loving and kind. One day he spies a poor beggar woman in the streets, and his life is never the same again.

item.title: What If World - Stories for Kids - 413. Maple asks: What if Fred went back in time to the Titanic? (w/ Mick Sullivan)
item.description:

Lessons include: You can’t change the past, but you can learn a lot from it; we have a responsibility to stand up against unjust rules… and to follow the ones that make sense (like don’t mess with time travel!).
